commands.review_summary:
The branch adds a process-local LINE per-user in-flight guard, wires it into `createLineBot`, sends a busy reply for stable-sender concurrent events, bypasses senderless events, and expands handler tests.

PR surface: Source +134, Tests +354. Total +488 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: no. live current-main reproduction was run in this read-only review. Source inspection shows current main has no per-user guard, and the PR body includes live LINE after-fix screenshots plus redacted logs.

target.title: feat(line): per-user in-flight guard for concurrent message errors
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When LINE users send rapid consecutive messages, the second message hits session lock timeouts or command queue contention, resulting in a generic "⚠️ Something went wrong" error after a long wait. The user gets no feedback for minutes, then sees an unhelpful error. ## Why This Change Was Made Instead of letting concurrent messages fail after a timeout, this adds a lightweight per-user in-flight guard at the LINE webhook handler level. When the same user's previous message is still being processed, the guard immediately sends a "⏳ still processing" reply and skips the duplicate, preventing the downstream concurrency conflict entirely. ## User Impact **This changes default LINE delivery semantics**: rapid follow-up events from the *same user* now get an immediate busy reply and are skipped, instead of dispatching concurrently and failing with a late timeout error. The guard is wired by default in `createLineBot`. - Users sending rapid messages get immediate "⏳ Your previous message is still being processed…" feedback instead of a timeout error - The guard only applies to events with a stable sender identity. `@line/bot-sdk` marks source `userId` optional (group/room postbacks and non-mobile group senders arrive without it), so senderless events bypass the guard and keep today's concurrent dispatch — one user's in-flight message can never block another user's button tap or message - Different users in the same group are isolated (guard key = account | conversation | user) - Guard releases on both success and error (try/finally), so a failed message never permanently blocks the user ## Evidence **Unit tests** — 35/35 pass (`pnpm test extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts`), covering: busy reply delivery, guard release after success/error, per-user isolation in groups, and regressions for senderless group postbacks/messages bypassing the guard. **Review findings addressed** (from the earlier Codex review): - Senderless postback cross-blocking: `buildLineInFlightKey` now returns `null` when `source.userId` is absent and the guard is skipped, so senderless group/room postbacks keep main's concurrent dispatch instead of collapsing onto one `unknown` key - The previous PR body incorrectly described the guard as opt-in; it is wired by default in `createLineBot` and the User Impact section above now states the delivery-semantics change explicitly - Rebased onto current `main`; conflicts resolved **Real LINE behavior proof** — captured on a live LINE Messaging API bot running this branch (commit `a3af9cd299`, since rebased to `5a59a2cbd6` with no code changes; gateway run from source, webhook via public tunnel). ## 1. Busy reply on rapid same-user messages (1:1 chat) Two messages sent back-to-back; the second immediately received the busy reply, then the first message's real answer arrived: ## 2. Same-group isolation + guard release (group chat) One group, two human users (green bubbles = user A, bee avatar = user B, penguin avatar = the bot): - 12:40 user A mentions the bot with a first message (processing takes ~10s) - 12:41 user A sends a rapid follow-up → gets the ⏳ busy reply (same-user guard) - user B's message sent during user A's processing is **not** blocked — no busy reply, normal answer (per-user isolation) - user A's later message is answered normally (guard released after completion) ## 3. Redacted gateway log timeline Guard-skipped messages never reach dispatch, so the second rapid message from the same user has no `message received` entry, while both distinct-user group messages do: ```text # 1:1 — first message dispatched and processed; the rapid second message was # guard-skipped before dispatch (no "message received" entry; busy reply in screenshot 1) 2026-07-06T12:35:47.495+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:U[redacted-user-A] messageId=621564378994966788 ... 2026-07-06T12:35:56.033+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:U[redacted-user-A] messageId=621564378994966788 outcome=completed duration=8537ms # group — two messages from two different users overlap; BOTH are dispatched # (different guard keys), the second queues and completes; no cross-user busy reply 2026-07-06T12:40:59.427+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564906756113015 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:00.868+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564907796299863 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:09.310+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564906756113015 outcome=completed duration=9881ms 2026-07-06T12:41:14.974+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564907796299863 outcome=completed duration=14099ms # group — user A's later message after guard release, answered normally 2026-07-06T12:41:16.583+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564936065122495 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:21.625+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564936065122495 outcome=completed duration=5042ms ``` User IDs, group ID, and session IDs are redacted. This PR supersedes openclaw/openclaw#96379 (same commits, resubmitted from this account); full review history and the original evidence comment are there.
